answer.rationale: Rollback is compliance-blocked despite memory_b1's strong track record, so that option is void regardless of its reliability. Regional failover (b2) and circuit breakers (b4) both risk dropping or diverting in-flight writes during a settlement peak, conflicting with the 'no lost writes' objective. Read-replica routing (b5) addresses read load, not the write-path latency actually climbing here, so it doesn't target the bottleneck. Memory_b3 describes provisioning headroom absorbing a peak surge with flat queue depth, which is the closest analog to heavy write load at daily peak, though that precedent was proactive (pre-peak) rather than reactive (mid-incident) — an imperfect match worth flagging rather than treating as guaranteed. Given payments/settlement is downstream-value-critical, I'm verifying b3's original record before committing capacity as the safest lever that doesn't touch the release or reroute live traffic.
